content.comment_body: Hello, Some mention that [article_no] is a replacement for another [article_no], while others claim that another [article_no] is outdated. I recently bought a new [article_no], and based on information from the [company_name] website, it appears this [article_no] is currently the only available model. If that's true, why doesn't this model allow using flags, when the older version supports up to 64 flags?

The [product_name] with article number [article_no] is in fact a recent version ([version_no]) and therefore a [article_no]. [company_name] has updated their article numbering system, which has led to quite a bit of confusion among users. This device is also capable of handling 64 digital flags. It's not necessary to choose [article_no] when selecting your device. In the selection menu, it appears as [product_name] [version_no].

analysis.insight_summary: Users experience confusion due to changes in [company_name]'s product naming and article numbering system, especially when trying to identify hardware versions and their features. Ambiguity regarding similar models results in misunderstandings about supported features like digital flags. Adjustments to product identifiers have increased uncertainty and user dissatisfaction.
analysis.user_expectations: Users seek straightforward identification of product versions and their feature sets, including clarity about backward compatibility—such as support for digital flags. They desire less ambiguity and expect features to be transparently documented and reliably available across different versions.
